$comment: Lunar corpus fixtures — real-world Lua projects swept by LuaCorpusSweepTest.
Each entry is a pinned upstream checkout fetched by fetch-corpus.py into test/corpus/<name>.
Pin to release tags (resolved to their commit SHA), never to a moving branch: the sweep is a
ratchet against a recorded baseline, so the tree must be byte-identical across runs.
NB: test/luacheck is a DIFFERENT tree — a clone of the internal glimmer/luacheck fork with
commits that do not exist upstream. It belongs to LuaRecursiveReferenceTest; do not conflate
the two.
Was corpus.tsv until 2026-08-05. Positional TSV was read by two hand-rolled parsers that
drifted: the shell bound 6 fields with IFS-whitespace collapsing (so every column after an
empty one shifted left, and `prune` became the language level, feeding an rm -rf), while the
Kotlin read 7 by index. JSON is parsed by a library on both sides — Python's stdlib `json` and
the platform's Gson — so no schema knowledge is hand-written anywhere. See BUG-407.
Fields:
name       directory under test/corpus/, and the baseline file name
url        upstream clone URL
commit     pinned SHA (a tag tip, resolved)
roots      subdirectories the sweep indexes — narrower than the checkout, so vendored and
build trees never enter the measurement
prune      optional; deleted after checkout so the builder rsync stays cheap
(luarocks/win32 alone is 11 MB of vendored Windows binaries)
luaLevel   the Lua language level the sweep runs under. It matters beyond the
LuaLanguageLevel inspection: the level selects which stdlib globals are known, so
an unpinned level would make every inspection count a function of
LuaProjectSettings' LUA54 default.
moduleRoot optional; the subdirectory module names resolve against, put on package.path for
the sweep. Omit when requires are relative to the checkout root, as all four below
are. It exists for projects that name modules relative to a subtree — KOReader's
require("ui/uimanager") means frontend/ui/uimanager.lua.
